# Step U: the bold colours by B

Lex (2026-11-07), on a prototype of two ways: "Can we hover the b and have options to change colors" → "Yes variant a", and "Where is the hover for colors on the b icon? I see them in the menu, where I don't want it, I want it on the hover with the b".

## What changes

- Hovering B on the selection bar, or reaching it with the keyboard, opens a small popover by it: **Bold text colour** (the default orange, five colours and a "+" for your own) and **Bold background** (None, five colours and a "+"), a sample word in the chosen look and **Reset**. Picking a colour changes how bold words look at once.
- Clicking B still only bolds or unbolds the selection. On a phone a tap on B bolds and opens the colours as well; a tap anywhere else closes them.
- They close when the pointer leaves B and the popover, on Escape (a second Escape closes the bar, as before), or when the keyboard focus leaves them. B has no tooltip any more, so nothing sits on them; its keys stay in `aria-keyshortcuts`.
- The popover never sits on the selected words: under the bar, over it, beside it, or at the top or bottom of what is seen, whichever comes first that keeps it on screen and off the words (`popSpot` in `public/edit-bar.js`). It is in the top layer, so the bar keeps its size. In a short window or with large text it is never taller than what is seen below the top bar, and scrolls inside itself.
- The two colour fields left the file name's menu: the colours live only by B now.
- The same saved setting: `script-editor:boldStyle` in this browser, per person (guests and hosts each keep their own). A colour chosen before keeps showing. The ready-made colours are `#rrggbb` (`BOLD_SWATCHES` in `public/cues.js`), so `boldStyle` keeps letting only those through. The default orange and None are "nothing chosen". **Reset** removes the saved setting: orange and bold, no background. (Step S had no Reset; Lex's approved prototype has one.)
- Each ready-made colour reads in both modes (release review, 2026-11-07): it is saved as its night colour, and light mode shows a darker partner on white (White becomes Black, the dark backgrounds become pale ones; `boldShown` in `public/cues.js`). To keep the default orange readable on it, the Yellow background is a pale yellow in dark mode too, and the four dark backgrounds are a little darker than in the prototype. Some text and background pairs still clash (Yellow text on the Yellow background, say). A background saved by the first build of step U (only ever on `dev`) counts as its new swatch (`was`). Every text colour has at least 3:1 against the page, and the default orange at least 3:1 on every background, in both modes. Your own colours show as picked in both modes.
- The keyboard: each row of colours is one Tab stop and the arrow keys move along it, so from B the input is at most four Tab presses away.
- Display only: no script text, prompter file or export changes.

## Checks

`tests/edit-bar.test.mjs` (`popSpot`, the bar's markup) and `tests/bold-always-on.test.mjs` (the colours by B and not in the menu, the swatches). In a real browser `scripts/smoke-keep-all.mjs` with `SMOKE_ONLY=look`: `runBoldLook` (the colours in dark and light mode, now read in the popover) and `runBoldPop` at 1280x800, 1280x420, 390x760 and 320x640: hover opens, the bar keeps its size, on screen and off the words, picking saves and shows at once, clicking B still bolds, your own colour, Reset, the pointer leaving, Escape, the keyboard, and on the phone sizes a tap on B, picking by tap and a tap elsewhere. `runMenuHeight` now checks New script is reachable and the menu has no colour fields. Evidence: `docs/agents/evidence/step-u-browser.txt`.

Not checked: a real phone, Firefox and Safari, and a colour field's own picker (the system's window; the check sets the field's value).

## Done

Feature list: updated (`docs/features.md`).

### Follow-ups

- Spec (P3): 3d9a6a8:public/app.js:1608 — P3 ticket: The spec says the colours close "when the pointer leaves B and the popover" (docs/build/step-u-bold-colours-by-b.md:9). After someone picks their own colour with the mouse through "+", that no longer holds. `popHeld` counts focus on a colour field (`f.type === "color"`) as holding the colours open. That's right while the system's colour window is open. But focus stays on the field after that window closes. So the `change` handler at public/app.js:1637 calls `closeBoldPopSoon`, which finds the colours still held. Every later `pointerleave` does the same. The colours stay open until a press somewhere else or Escape. This is a nit because it's a rarer path with a small cost: the colours sit off the words, and one click anywhere closes them. Fix: when a colour field fires `change` (its window has closed), move the focus off it unless it is `:focus-visible`. For example, `if (!e.target.matches(":focus-visible")) e.target.blur();` before `closeBoldPopSoon()`. Or hold only while a flag is set, from the field's `click` until its `change` or `blur`.
- Validation gaps (gap): Nothing covers the "+" mouse path after a pick. In `runBoldPop` (scripts/smoke-keep-all.mjs), after the step that sets the custom colour, add a check like the R1-4 one. Focus `#boldFg` with a mouse click, set its value and fire `input` and `change` as the existing check does, then move the pointer to (4, height−4). Use `page.until(\`!${popOpen}\`, …, 1500)` and check that the bar is still open. With the fix above this passes; today it would time out.
- Validation gaps (gap): The ArrowLeft wrap is not really checked. In scripts/smoke-keep-all.mjs:1273-1276, Home is pressed straight after ArrowLeft, and Home always goes to the default swatch. So the check passes even if ArrowLeft did nothing or went to the wrong place. The fix: after `pressKey(page, "ArrowLeft", …)`, wait 40 ms and check `(await focused()) === "boldFg"` (ArrowLeft from the first swatch should wrap to the row's colour field). Only then press Home and keep the existing check.
- Spec (P3): 5a8f408:docs/build/step-u-bold-colours-by-b.md:31 — P3 ticket: The "Follow-ups" list still says the ArrowLeft wrap is not really checked. This slice fixes that: scripts/smoke-keep-all.mjs:1285-1286 now waits and checks `focused() === "boldFg"` before Home is pressed, and the evidence file has "ArrowLeft at the start wraps to the row's end" at both sizes. Fix: remove that follow-up, or mark it done in 5a8f408. Also add one line to "Checks" (line 19) for the new large-text, short-window check in `runBoldPop`.
- Spec (P3): 5a8f408:docs/build/step-u-bold-colours-by-b.md:10 — P3 ticket: The same bullet now promises two things that can't both hold. It says the popover "never sits on the selected words", then that it is "never taller than what is seen below the top bar". When the height cap applies, the popover is exactly as tall as the room below the top bar, so `popSpot` (public/edit-bar.js:146) finds no spot above or below that stays off the words. It falls back to `spots[0]` or `spots[1]`, which get clamped to `low` and cover the words. Before this change it also overlapped, and ran off screen, so this is not a regression. But the spec now reads as if both are always true. Fix: say in the bullet that when the colours are capped to the full height they may cover the words, and that they scroll inside.
- Standards (P3): 5a8f408:public/app.js:1597 — P3 style: The new lines work out the top edge and the visual viewport bottom for the popover's height. Line 1601 then works out the same two values again as `v`/`top`, and line 1602 repeats the `vh` expression. Fix: compute `v`, `top` and `vh` once at the start of `placeBoldPop`. Use them for `--pop-room-y` (`vh - top - 2 * EDGE`, or the existing 16) and pass the same values to `popSpot`. Then the cap and the placement can't drift apart.
- Validation gaps (gap): The new browser check (scripts/smoke-keep-all.mjs:1199-1200) asserts `tall.top >= 0`, but the spec says "below the top bar". A popover that slid under the top bar would still pass. Return `document.querySelector(".top").getBoundingClientRect().bottom` in the same `page.eval` and check `tall.top >= topBottom`.
- Validation gaps (gap): The check only runs at 1280x420 (`height <= 420`). The phone sizes, where the visual viewport is used and an on-screen keyboard shrinks it, are not covered. Run the same block at 320x640 too, with a font size that overflows there (say 300%).
